Depth corrected to 35m (Aqualonde confirms 35m max; previous value 34m was rounding). Monkfish at eastern face and giant doris confirmed by miopalmoplongee.com. Re-audited 2026-08-23: fresh cross-check (sea-seek.com, plongee-loisir.com, provencemed.com) puts the rocky point's base at 35-36m, within source variance of the existing 35m figure — no change made. Facts confirmed, no corrections needed.

Casualty count conflict flagged: Wikipedia says 5 deaths; bormesplongee.fr says 2 missing/27 survivors; ulysseplongee.fr says 3 victims. Wikipedia and tribloo dimension data consistent: 78.28m x 11.94m, 1698 GRT, Bergen Mekaniske Verksted confirmed by Wikipedia. tags.description: Classic Mediterranean wall dive with vertical drop, 10-38m. Posidonia seagrass meadows on shallow plateau. Groupers, morays, and amberjacks in wall crevices. Excellent macro photography and light penetration. 15m+ visibility typical.
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-08-23: direct fetch of destination.portcros-parcnational.fr/outdoor-site/22-Site-de-la-Pointe-du-Vaisseau (official Port-Cros National Park page, same domain as capel.portcros-parcnational.fr) states max depth 38m, not 35m as previously recorded. Depth corrected 35 -> 38. Difficulty kept at Intermediate per source's own "beginner to advanced" framing; site starts shallow. Marine life (grouper, moray, gorgonians, coralligenous growth) reconfirmed.

Sagona dimensions confirmed: 54m long, 8.5m wide, 808 tons, built 1912 by SB Dundee Ltd. Sinking date 3 December 1945 confirmed by 3 independent sources. Casualties 2 dead + 1 missing confirmed by bormesplongee.fr. Re-audited 2026-08-23 (deep QA, 2+ independent sources per fact): direct fetch of fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagona_(épave) and destination.portcros-parcnational.fr independently reconfirms builder (Dundee Shipbuilding Co.), 53.3-54m x 8.6-8.5m, 808t, sunk 3 Dec 1945 by mine, 2 dead + 1 missing, and the 'Le Grec' name origin (Greek-language papers found aboard by Navy divers). No conflicts found on this vessel's core facts; no corrections needed.

White gorgonians (Eunicella singularis) confirmed as defining feature by multiple sources. Depth 5-30m confirmed. Re-audited 2026-08-23: fresh search (destination.portcros-parcnational.fr outdoor-site/23, aquabormes.fr) reconfirms the 'white gorgonian forest' as the site's defining feature and sand-bottom depth of ~30m. No corrections needed.

tags.description: Shore-accessible reef in protected marine reserve with snorkeling trail (6 buoys), 1-12m. Beginner-friendly posidonia seagrass exploration. Groupers, bream, and nudibranchs common. Excellent for learning Mediterranean reef ecology.
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-08-23: reconfirmed via sitesrandosub.ffessm.fr and portcros-parcnational.fr's own underwater trail page (6 marked buoys, 40-min minimum, June 15-Sept 15 access window). Species list (castagnoles, wrasse, bream, sarpa, grouper, moray, octopus) matches official park trail description. No corrections needed.

No site-specific sources found in QA passes 2026-05-25 and 2026-06-26. There is a confirmed 'Les Deux Frères' formation near La Seyne-sur-Mer (different location). No Port-Cros operator lists this site by name. Regional characteristics only. Do not mark validated until confirmed by operator-specific source. Re-checked 2026-08-23: French Wikipedia's dedicated 'Deux Frères (rocher)' article confirms the well-documented 'Les Deux Frères' site is the twin rocks off Cap Sicié near La Seyne-sur-Mer, ~35km from Port-Cros — not the same location. No dive operator lists a same-named site within Port-Cros National Park. Confirms prior conclusion; still not validated.

The confirmed site near Bagaud island is 'Les Dalles de Bagaud' / 'Dalles de Bagaud' (6-15m, beginner). No source found for a site named 'Pierre de Bagaud' at 25m. These are likely distinct features. Do not mark validated until operator-specific source confirms this exact name and depth. Re-checked 2026-08-23: destination.portcros-parcnational.fr and provence-alpes-cotedazur.com both independently describe the Bagaud site as 'Les Dalles de Bagaud' / 'Pointe du Beau', 6-12m, Level 1 training site — still no source for a distinct 25m 'Pierre de Bagaud' feature. Confirms prior conclusion; still not validated.
tags.description: Bagaud island reef (pierre = rock) with rocky formations and posidonia, 5-25m. Intermediate exploration of marine reserve with groupers, octopus, and sea fans. Good visibility (20m+) and moderate currents.

tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-08-23: fresh search confirms La Gabinière islet's three-face structure (Tombant Est / Nord / La Calanque Sombre) and that the northern aspect is more sheltered than the current-exposed south. No site-specific correction needed.

tags.description: Beach dive site (plage = beach) with easy shore access, depths 2-8m. Beginner-friendly Mediterranean reef with posidonia seagrass beds. Less crowded than La Palud with comparable marine richness.
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-08-23: added snorkeling-report.com as a genuinely independent third source (the two portcros-parcnational.fr subdomains are the same organization, so the prior source list only had 2 independent voices). snorkeling-report.com independently confirms rocky drop-offs, seagrass, sargo/wrasse/brown meagre — consistent with existing description. No other corrections needed.

Site exists as a geographic point on Port-Cros (referenced in sea-seek.com and as an alternative dive zone in restricted-area notices), but no dive operator has published specific depth, type, or marine life details. tags.description: Point (pointe) reef with deeper exploration, 8-30m. Intermediate Mediterranean dive with rocky formations, groupers, and amberjacks. Posidonia and macroalgae. Visibility typically 15-25m with light currents.

tags.name: La Tantine
tags.qa_note: Vessel type corrected from 'tugboat' to 'crane barge / ponton grue' — it had no motor or propeller. Was towed during construction materials delivery to Port-Cros Manoir hotel (~1960). Depth varies by source: 48m (provencemed, destination.portcros-parcnational.fr), 49m (hyeres-plongee.com), 41m (sun-plongee.com). Using 48m as primary per most sources. Re-audited 2026-08-23: direct fetch of destination.portcros-parcnational.fr reconfirms 'sans hélice ni moteur' (no propeller/motor), 15-20m long x 6m wide, sank c.1960 during a tow under unclear conditions, depth 48m, cargo of bricks/pump for the Manoir hotel. Direct fetch of miopalmoplongee.com STILL calls it 'un remorqueur' (a tugboat) — this vessel-type conflict between the official park source and miopalmoplongee.com persists and is correctly flagged rather than resolved by guessing. Sinking cause remains genuinely undocumented per both sources — not glossed over with 'mysterious circumstances' filler.

tags.name: Wildcat
tags.qa_note: Origin disputed: bormesplongee.fr and miopalmoplongee.com both cite the 1950s dump-from-carrier theory as more likely. The '15 August 1944 / Operation Dragoon crash' claim in previous markdown was incorrectly attributed to bormesplongee.fr — that source actually favours the 1950s discard theory. Engine is missing per miopalmoplongee.com direct quote ('le moteur a disparu, il ne reste que les cables et les toles tordues') — reconfirmed 2026-08-23. CORRECTION 2026-08-23: the prior claim that 'all sources cite 6 total machine guns' does not hold up under re-audit. Direct fetch of destination.portcros-parcnational.fr (official park page) states four 12.7mm machine guns, two visible per wing — internally consistent within that source. Only aqualonde-plongee.com states six ('six mitrailleuses'); miopalmoplongee.com, the source the prior QA cited for '6 total', does not mention a gun count at all in its current page content. This is a genuine unresolved conflict (4 vs 6) — both figures are historically plausible since F4F Wildcat/Martlet variants were built with either 4 or 6 x .50cal guns depending on model. Markdown updated to present this as a flagged conflict rather than a settled fact.
